name: Import from DICE
description: Bring an organization's DICE events, ticket holders and fans into Exos, read only from DICE's partner Ticket Holders API (GraphQL queries only; Exos never writes to DICE). An owner or manager connects once in Org settings → Integrations by pasting the API token generated in MIO, DICE's partner dashboard; the token is stored in Vault and never returned by any route. Each upcoming DICE event becomes a **draft link-out event** (`ticket_backend` `dice`): Exos lists it and sends buyers to DICE, and never sells its inventory. Each DICE ticket of such an event becomes an entry on the event's `DICE` door list carrying its DICE code, so the holder's DICE barcode scans at the Exos door; a DICE return voids it. Buyers and holders become fans; a fan joins the organization's email list **only** when DICE's `optInPartners` is true. The first sync reads everything; later syncs read what changed since the last one (events by `updatedAt`, orders by `purchasedAt`, returns by `returnedAt`, transfers by `transferredAt`), and a sync stopped by its caps resumes where it stopped. Re-running never duplicates anything. Field-by-field mapping: docs/dice-coverage.md. Needs `org:admin`; behind the `EXOS_DICE_IMPORT` switch (503 when off).

endpoints.description: Whether DICE is connected (`status`: not_connected, connected, error when DICE refused the token, disconnected), the DICE account's name, when it last synced and whether a sync is running, each entity's incremental cursor (`since`; `resuming` when a capped pass is part way), what was imported (`events` created in Exos, `events_past` recorded only, door entries, orders, fans and how many of them have marketing consent from DICE) and the last run. Never the token.

responses.description: Import from DICE is switched off on this install (EXOS_DICE_IMPORT is not on).

example.error: Import from DICE is switched off on this Exos install (EXOS_DICE_IMPORT). Ask the operator to turn it on.

endpoints.description: Every sync and dry run, newest first: `kind` (full or incremental), `trigger` (dashboard, api, cron), `dry_run`, `status` (running, ok, partial when a cap stopped it and the next run resumes, error), the counts per entity (`read`, `created`, `updated`, `past`, `no_event`, `voided`, `pending`, `fans_created`, `fans_consented`, `errors` …; a dry run's `preview`), DICE's warnings and the error.

parameters.name: page
parameters.description: Page number, 1-10000 (default 1). A page past the end answers an empty data array.

example.error: Import from DICE is switched off on this Exos install (EXOS_DICE_IMPORT). Ask the operator to turn it on.

endpoints.description: Runs one sync and answers when it is done (up to about 100 seconds): the full first read until it has completed once, incremental after. A run reads at most 40 pages of 50 per entity and 5,000 rows in all; `result` `partial` means the next run (another call, the dashboard or the hourly schedule) continues where this one stopped. `dry_run: true` reads the same way (at most 4 pages per entity) and writes nothing but its log row: `preview` says how many upcoming and past events, ticket types, tickets, orders, returns and transfers it read and how many distinct fans, of whom how many would get marketing consent. Runs as the member who created the key, who must be an owner or manager; needs an organization API key. Every check (the key's member, the role, a running sync or preview, the limits) happens before Exos sends anything to DICE. One sync at a time per organization and at most one a minute; one dry run at a time, none while a sync runs, five a minute.
